record.original_question: Let (X, H) be a smooth complex projective polarized variety. Does there always exist a class gamma in the numerical Chow ring of the form gamma = e^{-B} * (1, 0, Gamma, gamma_3, ..., gamma_n) together with an upper semicontinuous function f^gamma: R -> R such that every gamma-tilt-semistable object E satisfies the quadratic inequality Q_{s,q}(E) >= 0 for all (s, q) in Delta with q > f^gamma(s)?

evidence.quote: (4.6) gamma := e^{-B} * (1, 0, Gamma, gamma3 , . . . , gamman ) in CH_num(X) tensor R ... and set ch^gamma(-) := gamma * ch(-).

Conjecture 4.13 (Bayer-Macri). Let (X, H) be a smooth complex projective polarized variety. There exists a class gamma as in (4.6) and an upper semicontinuous function f := f^gamma : R -> R such that, for any sigma^gamma_{s,q}-semistable object E, Q_{s,q}(E) := q((v1^gamma)^2 - 2v0^gamma v2^gamma) + s(3v0^gamma v3^gamma - v1^gamma v2^gamma) + (2(v2^gamma)^2 - 3v1^gamma v3^gamma) >= 0, for all (s, q) in Delta, such that q > f^gamma(s).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,H)$ be a smooth complex projective polarized variety of dimension $n$, and let $\mathrm{CH}_{\mathrm{num}}(X)_{\mathbb{R}}$ denote its numerical Chow ring with real coefficients. Fix a real divisor class $B$ on $X$ and choose a class
$$\gamma = e^{-B}\cdot(1,\,0,\,\Gamma,\,\gamma_3,\dots,\gamma_n)\in\mathrm{CH}_{\mathrm{num}}(X)_{\mathbb{R}},$$
where $\Gamma\in\mathrm{CH}^2_{\mathrm{num}}(X)_{\mathbb{R}}$ and $\gamma_i\in\mathrm{CH}^i_{\mathrm{num}}(X)_{\mathbb{R}}$ for $i\ge 3$. For an object $E$ in $D^b(X)$ define the twisted Chern character $\mathrm{ch}^\gamma(E):=\gamma\cdot\mathrm{ch}(E)$, and write $v_i^\gamma(E):=H^{n-i}\cdot\mathrm{ch}^\gamma_i(E)\in\mathbb{R}$ for $i=0,1,2,3$. For $(s,q)$ in the standard region
$$\Delta=\{(s,q)\in\mathbb{R}^2: q>s^2\},$$
there is an associated weak stability condition $\sigma^\gamma_{s,q}$ (the tilt-stability built from $\gamma$, $H$, and the parameters $s,q$). Define the quadratic form
$$Q_{s,q}(E):=q\bigl((v_1^\gamma)^2-2v_0^\gamma v_2^\gamma\bigr)+s\bigl(3v_0^\gamma v_3^\gamma-v_1^\gamma v_2^\gamma\bigr)+\bigl(2(v_2^\gamma)^2-3v_1^\gamma v_3^\gamma\bigr).$$

Question: Does there exist, for every such $(X,H)$, a choice of class $\gamma$ as above together with an upper semicontinuous function $f^\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for every $\sigma^\gamma_{s,q}$-semistable object $E$ one has
$$Q_{s,q}(E)\ge 0\quad\text{for all }(s,q)\in\Delta\text{ with }q>f^\gamma(s)?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker (Bayer–Macrì) quadratic inequality for tilt-semistable objects is known to be a long-standing conjecture for general smooth projective threefolds (and higher-dimensional polarized varieties). It has been verified for various special cases (e.g. Fano threefolds of Picard rank 1, abelian threefolds, certain Calabi–Yau threefolds such as complete intersections of quadric and quartic), but disproved in its strongest original form for some blow-ups, prompting the modified ("twisted by $\gamma$") version posed here. No proof of the general statement is available; it remains open.

status_evidence.title: Stability condition on Calabi–Yau threefold of complete intersection of quadratic and quartic hypersurfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the Bayer–Macrì–Toda conjectural BG-type inequality in a particular Calabi-Yau threefold case.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is proved only in special cases, indicating the general statement is still open.

status_evidence.title: Bridgeland stability conditions on threefolds I (Bayer–Macrì–Toda)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces the conjectural Bogomolov–Gieseker-type inequality for tilt-stable complexes on threefolds.
status_evidence.claim: Original formulation of the conjecture; the general case remains a conjecture.

status_evidence.title: A generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker inequality for the smooth quadric threefold
status_evidence.snippet: Verifies the conjecture in the case of the quadric threefold.
status_evidence.claim: Verification in special cases only supports that the general conjecture is open.
